idiom_name: controller + dispatcher mapping + command-like workers + view helper + view template
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give every request one entry point (controller) that performs the shared work - session and locale resolution, authentication, validation, error mapping - and a dispatcher that turns the logical outcome of the request into the next view. The unit of work is a command-like worker: it calls the business/application layer, updates state and populates an intermediate model, then reports which view should render. Views and their helpers consume that model and contain no retrieval or business logic. What the pattern fixes is ordering and ownership: processing happens before view selection, and view selection is a single decision instead of a per-view accident.
code_sketch:
request -> controller
  dispatcher.resolve(request)         # which worker? which view?
  worker = dispatcher.worker_for(request)
  model  = worker.service(request)    # business tier call + intermediate model
  view   = dispatcher.view_for(model, request)   # success/error/fragment view
render(view, model)                   # helpers may adapt, never retrieve
pitfalls: Deferring content retrieval to render time (helpers or templates querying services) turns the implementation into the sibling Dispatcher View strategy and doubles the work when the worker also fetched data.
The intermediate model degrades into an untyped bag of keys that the worker writes and the view hopes to read; without a typed view model the contract drifts silently.
Business logic migrating into the worker/controller duplicates the application-service layer instead of orchestrating it.

Wrong move: relying on string view names and untyped model keys wired together only at request time -> a renamed template or mistyped action name resolves to nothing and fails as a 500 or a blank page while serving traffic instead of at build time -> instead centralise view names in constants or typed result objects (Spring ViewResolver chain configuration, ASP.NET strongly-typed View<TModel>) and add a smoke test that walks the dispatcher mapping to every real view.

Wrong move: the worker returns fully-rendered HTML (or the action writes the response body itself) because it is one step quicker -> the dispatcher can no longer substitute an error, fragment or export view for the same outcome, so every alternate channel needs a duplicate worker -> instead have the worker return a typed outcome plus model and let the dispatcher select the template.

Wrong move: putting per-page conditionals into shared middleware/filters or the dispatcher itself because that is where the request object is at hand -> the routing layer accretes authentication edge cases, data fetches and navigation branches until it is a single untestable chokepoint affecting every request (the fat-controller failure moved one layer earlier) -> instead keep filters generic and cross-cutting and push per-request decisions into the worker that owns that request kind.
